## Step 3
```{python}
def clean_transcript(file):
    lines = file.read_text(encoding="utf-8-sig").splitlines()
    cleaned = []

    for line in lines:
        if line.startswith(("*CHI:", "*INV:")):
            speaker, speech = line.split(":", 1)

            speech = re.sub("r\x15.*?\x15", " ", speech)
            speech = re.sub(r"\[[^\]]*\]", " ", speech)
            speech = re.sub(r"&[=+\-]?\S+", " ", speech)
            speech = re.sub(r"\b(?:xxx|yyy|www)\b", " ", speech, flags=re.I)
            speech = re.sub(r"\b\d+_\d+\b", " ", speech)
            speech = re.sub(r"[^\w\s']", " ", speech)
            speech = re.sub(r"\s+", " ", speech).strip().lower()

            if speech: 
                cleaned.append(f"{speaker}: {speech}")

    return cleaned 

for file in files:
    cleaned = clean_transcript(file)

    print(file.name)
    print("Toatl utterances:", len(cleaned))
    print("First 10 utterances:")

    for line in cleaned[:10]:
        print(line)

    print()

for file in files:
    cleaned = clean_transcript(file)

    child_lines = [
        line for line in cleaned
        if line.startswith("*CHI")
    ]

    print(file.name)
    print("Child utterances:", len(child_lines))
    print("First 10 cleaned child utterances:")

    for line in child_lines[:10]:
        print(line)

    print()
```

rows = []

for file in files:

        rows.append({
            "child": file.stem,
            "speaker": speaker,
            "utterances": speech.strip()

## Deliverables 

## 1. The Raw Data 
I used two child langauge transcripts from the Elis Weismer collection in the CHILDES database. One transcript is from a late talking child, and the other is from a typically dveloping child. Both children were aorund 2 and a half years old. The transcripts contain conversations between the child and an investigator. I kept the same data source from component one. Source: <https://talkbank.org/childes/access/Clinical-Eng/EllisWeismer.html>

## 2. Cleaning Steps 
I first loaded both .cha files into python. I removed headers, timestamps, and other symbold that were not neccessary. I kept the lines spoken by the child (*CHI) and investigator(*INV) so I could keep the conversation between them. I also removed letters that were not words like "XXX". I converated the whole text to lowercase. One step I made was removing nonwords. That made it easier to count and compare the actual words, but also means some of what teh child said was not able to transcribe. 

## 3. The Clean Table 
Each row represents one cleaned utterance from either the child or investigator. The child column identifies which transcript the utterance came from. The speaker column shows whether the child or investigator was speaking. The utterances column contains the cleaned speech. There is around 600 rows. 

## 4. Still Messy 
Words like "where's" and "that's" could affect my word count. I need to decide how to identify verbs and count unique words. I removed timestamps and some transcript that could have provided additional information, but they were not necccessary.
